Subject: Hosted API — quick clarifications on data residency and deletion

Hi Karthik,

Our security team had a few follow-ups specifically about how Redwood’s hosted API handles customer data for live requests: residency, retention windows, and what the deletion workflow looks like for both cached artifacts and persisted logs. They want short, actionable answers to include in our internal review.

Could you please confirm: 1) whether request/response payloads can be pinned to a US-only region for storage and logs, 2) default retention period for request logs and evidence of deletion, and 3) the standard process and SLA for a full customer data wipe if we request it?

Appreciate a concise reply we can pass to the compliance group.

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear asks. Below are concise answers your compliance team can paste into their questionnaire. Attaching a short evidence pack and a one-page retention summary.

1) Region pinning (logs & request artifacts):
- For hosted API customers we support region affinity for request logs and stored artifacts in our hosted offering in supported regions. For US-only residency choose the "US region" during onboarding; all request logs and short-term artifacts will be kept in US regions only (no cross-region replication for those artifacts).

2) Default retention windows:
- Request/response logs (metadata + payloads): default retention 30 days.
- Short-term inference cache (KV/prefix caches used to accelerate inference): ephemeral and evicted within minutes to hours depending on workload; cache snapshot backups are retained up to 7 days for operational recovery.
- Long-term observability metrics/traces: 90 days retention unless a longer retention add-on is purchased.

3) Deletion / bulk wipe process and SLA:
- Customer-initiated immediate wipe: upon formal request (support ticket + authorized signature from the account owner), we trigger a three-stage wipe: 1) eviction of inference caches and session state (near-immediate), 2) purge of request logs and artifacts from primary storage (initiated within 24 hours), 3) removal from backups/snapshots during the next scheduled backup compaction cycle (within 30 days).
- SLA: primary storage purge completion typically within 72 hours; full purge from all backup tiers within 30 days. We provide an execution log and verification report when complete.

Additional notes: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant and maintain tamper-evident audit logs. For customers requiring stricter controls we offer Dedicated and Private deployments (customer-managed KMS) — on hosted API, encryption at rest uses Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed keys are available as an enterprise add-on.

Attachments: aureline_survey_answers_v1.pdf, aureline_evidence_pack_v1.zip

If you want, Kimberly and I can jump on a 20m call with your compliance team to walk through the evidence pack.

Best,

Hi Sofia — quick follow-up with two clarifications your team often asks for when documenting vendor behavior: 

- "Default retention 30 days" above includes both raw request payload (if customer has not enabled optional persistence) and the generated text outputs. If a customer enables persistent storage for audit or logging reasons we record that as "persisted by customer opt-in" and retention follows the configured tenant policy.

- For emergency legal holds we can suspend scheduled deletion for a named tenant while preserving the standard deletion hygiene once the hold is released; we provide the legal hold request and release audit trail. That process is handled via our account support flow and requires the account owner or legal contact to authorize.

Happy to provide the exact sentence your compliance team prefers; a common line we provide is: "Redwood’s hosted API stores request/response logs by default for 30 days; customers may enable extended retention or opt-out of persistence. On verified customer request Redwood will purge primary storage artifacts within 72 hours and complete backup purges within 30 days, with a deletion verification report provided."

—Kimberly
Senior Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
